examples.text: Tu es un battant, un gagnant!

examples.text: Même une catastrophe, c'est juste un accroc!
examples.trans: Even a disaster is just a hitch!

examples.text: Pour Gabriel, même une catastrophe, c'est juste un accroc!
examples.trans: For Gabriel, even a disaster is just a hitch!

meanings.note: before a noun: ce film, cette tête, ces gens
as a pronoun in c'est, ce n'est pas; becomes c' before a vowel

examples.text: La plus grande imprésario de Paris.

dire la vérité à quelqu'un = to tell someone the truth

examples.trans: The agency isn't going to disappear.

meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to disappear'.

falloir.governs: il faut + infinitive, or il faut que + subjunctive

meanings.note: only with the impersonal 'il': il faut
il me faut un stylo = I need a pen
First-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are'), the most productive verb class in French. Core French verb meaning 'congratulate'.

examples.text: Tu es un battant, un gagnant!

examples.trans: The winners are always on the end!

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: before the verb: vous la connaissez? les voilà

meanings.en: to raise, lift (se lever = to get up, stand up)
meanings.note: First-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are'), the most productive verb class in French. Core French verb meaning 'raise, get up'.

examples.text: José? Il faut te lever maintenant!
examples.trans: Jose? You have to get up now!

meanings.note: in speech: elle est là = she's here; je suis là = I'm here

meanings.note: past participle of mourir, used as an adjective
ne ... pas: not; ne ... plus: not anymore; ne ... jamais: never
no object: je pars = I'm leaving

examples.text: Oui, Cécile est un peu plus âgée.
examples.trans: Yes, Cécile is a little older.

meanings.en: un peu = a little, a bit

examples.text: Je suis là pour voir Mathias.

examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: before an infinitive: pour faire plaisir

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.

examples.text: Disons, le reste de ma vie.

examples.trans: Don't just stay there doing nothing!

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.

meanings.note: agrees with the thing owned, not the owner

singular and informal: friends, family, children, colleagues of the same age

meanings.note: + noun: je veux un café; + infinitive: je veux partir

examples.text: S'il vous plaît. Il n'y a rien entre Mathias et moi, d'accord?
